prerequisites: Solid background in the analysis of analog electronic circuits.
Solid background in various electronic devices.
"Dispositivos electrónicos y fotónicos" (Electronic and Photonic Devices) course.
"Fundamentos de Electrónica Analógica" (Fundamentals of Analog Electronics) course.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand and evaluate the process of generation, transport, distribution and storage of electrical energy, with special emphasis on generation and storage processes for remote applications.
Analyze and size the protection systems of a simple low voltage installation.

Understand the characteristics that distinguish power diodes and MOSFET transistors from signal ones and understand the operation of other electronic devices used exclusively in power applications (IGBTs, SCRs, Triacs and GTOs).
Understand the operation of uncontrolled single-phase and three-phase rectifiers and calculate the voltages and currents in their components.
Analyze, quantify and design linear power supplies.
Understand the operation of basic DC/DC converters and single-phase DC/AC converters and calculate the voltages and currents in their components.
Analyze the operation of simple power electronic systems of special interest in the world of telecommunications.
Perform simulation of general purpose electronic circuits with computer tools.
Select semiconductor devices and power capacitors for a known application.
Calculate power magnetic components (coils and transformers) for a known application.
Understand the operation of controlled and semi-controlled single-phase and three-phase rectifiers and calculate the voltages and currents in their components.

syllabus_topics: The electrical energy distribution network: Structure of electrical systems, electric energy generation, transmission and distribution facilities, analysis of three-phase systems.
Other sources of electrical energy: Wind energy conversion, solar radiation, solar concentrators, solar thermal energy (ovens and thermal solar plants), photovoltaic cells, fuel cells.

Electrical energy storage systems: Characteristics, charging and maintenance of batteries, other electrical energy storage systems (flywheels, superconducting coils, and ultracapacitors), influence of these systems on the current electrical distribution scheme and the environment.
Principles of AC-DC conversion: Uncontrolled single-phase rectifiers, filters for AC component elimination, uncontrolled polyphase rectifiers.
Linear power supplies: Basic structure, unregulated voltage stabilizers, feedback voltage stabilizers, design of linear power supplies.
Principles of switched DC-DC conversion: Pulse width modulators, basic converters without galvanic isolation, basic converters with galvanic isolation, converters with multiple transistors.
Principles of DC-AC conversion: Basic single-phase inverter structures, pulse width modulations for inverters, filters for harmonic elimination.

Electronic devices for power electronic converters: Power diode, power MOSFET transistor, insulated gate bipolar transistor (IGBT), passive elements in power electronic converters (transformers, coils, and capacitors), influence of these elements on energy efficiency and the environment, thermal protection circuits.

Examples of power electronic systems for telecommunications: Introduction to uninterruptible power supply systems (UPSs), power supply systems in telephone exchanges, power supply systems for digital processors, role of these systems in the connected society of the future.
teaching_methods: Analysis and design of power electronic circuits

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory practices (tasks and final practical exam)
Theoretical part - Block 3.A (Topics 3-9, part A) written test
Theoretical part - Block 3.B (Topics 3-9, part B) written test

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated as 20% Laboratory Practices (PL) + 80% Theory, provided that a minimum of 3 out of 10 points is achieved in each evaluable component (B1, B2, B3.A, B3.B, and PL components). The Theory grade is 18%·B1 + 12%·B2 + 20%·B3.A + 50%·B3.B. If minimums are not met, the course is failed, and the final grade is the minimum between 4 and the weighted sum. Unsuccessful theory blocks (B1, B2, B3.A) can be re-evaluated in the ordinary call, taking the maximum score. For the extraordinary call, the PL grade is retained, and theoretical blocks with unmet minimums from the ordinary call must be re-evaluated in a single comprehensive exam for B1, B2, and B3. If B3.A or B3.B from the ordinary call failed, B3 must be fully re-evaluated. If PL was not evaluated in the ordinary call, it receives 0 points in the extraordinary call.
